tasks.title: Dispatcher fan-out changed to first-subscriber-only dispatch
tasks.phase_a_question: Trace EventBus.post -> Dispatcher.dispatch -> Subscriber.dispatchEvent -> invokeSubscriberMethod. Explain why dispatch fans out to all matching subscribers instead of stopping after one subscriber, and what isolation/performance tradeoff that design makes.
tasks.phase_b_question: Dispatcher.dispatch was changed so ImmediateDispatcher delivers an event only to the first matching subscriber. Evaluate the impact: what design property was lost, which downstream path is skipped, and what performance/isolation tradeoff was made?

tasks.title: Subscriber.dispatchEvent renamed without updating dispatchers
tasks.phase_a_question: Trace EventBus.post through the dispatcher to Subscriber.dispatchEvent. Explain why the async/executor boundary is hidden behind Subscriber.dispatchEvent rather than forcing Dispatcher implementations to know executor details.
tasks.phase_b_question: Subscriber.dispatchEvent was renamed to enqueueEventForDispatch but dispatcher callers were not updated. Which upstream callers/dependencies are now broken, and what design separation did the old dispatchEvent boundary enforce?

tasks.title: Async handoff moved above queue drain
tasks.phase_a_question: Trace AsyncEventBus.post through Dispatcher.legacyAsync and Subscriber.dispatchEvent. Explain exactly where the async boundary is and why queue drain stays on the posting thread.
tasks.phase_b_question: A bug report says AsyncEventBus now returns before the legacy dispatch queue is drained. Diagnose which design boundary moved, what ordering guarantee changed, and where to inspect in the chain.
